findings.current: Hong had once heard that the terrifying Fire King had personally torn apart and killed a thousand vicious Demonic Cult fiends.
findings.defect: The modifier meaning “terrifying” describes the Demonic Cult in the source, but the draft transfers it to the Fire King.
findings.rationale: The replacement restores the source’s attribution while preserving that the Fire King acted alone.
findings.replacement: Hong had once heard that the Fire King had single-handedly torn apart and killed a thousand vicious fiends of the terrifying Demonic Cult.
findings.source: 일전에 듣기로는 그 무서운 마교의 흉신악살 천 명을 단신으로 찢어 죽였다고도 했다.

findings.current:
“……”

“You’re becoming more insane by the day. Is there something wrong with your Fire Gate Divine Technique?”
findings.defect: A single continuous utterance has been split into two separate dialogue paragraphs, making the initial pause appear to be its own speech turn.
findings.rationale: The ellipsis leads directly into the old man’s sentence in the source.
findings.replacement: “…You’re becoming more insane by the day. Is there something wrong with your Fire Gate Divine Technique?”
findings.source: “……갈수록 미친놈이 되어 가는군. 열화신공에 문제라도 있었나?”

findings.current: “Puhahaha! He thinks you’re a Mountain Spirit. Old Man, wasn’t it three months ago that you forgot your formula while circulating your qi and almost became a ghost?”
findings.defect: “Old Man” makes Taekyung’s address sound casually disrespectful and discards the established hierarchical address represented by 노야.
findings.rationale: Taekyung is teasing Jeok Cheongang, but he still addresses his overwhelming elder and master with the established private form “Old Master.”
findings.replacement: “Puhahaha! He thinks you’re a Mountain Spirit. Old Master, wasn’t it three months ago that you forgot your formula while circulating your qi and almost became a ghost?”
findings.source: “푸하하! 신령이래. 노야, 석 달 전인가, 운기조식하다가 구결 까먹어서 유령 될 뻔하지 않았어요?”

findings.current: His calm attitude and tone were so incongruous that even the massive trees snapped to pieces behind him seemed insignificant.
findings.defect: The sentence is grammatically malformed and obscures the contrast: his nonchalance makes the destruction behind him seem inconsequential.
findings.rationale: The source contrasts his utterly casual demeanor with the conspicuous destruction caused by the blow.
findings.replacement: His manner and tone were so nonchalant that the massive trees that had been snapped apart behind him might as well not have been there.
findings.source: 그의 뒤로 와지끈 부러져 있는 아름드리나무들이 무색해질 정도로 태연한 태도와 말투였다.

findings.current: “Sichuan is fun, isn’t it? I studied hard during evening self-study there.”[^3]
findings.defect: The draft mistakes 사천성 for the province alone and changes Taekyung’s action from playing the tile-matching game of the same name during evening self-study to studying in Sichuan. This invents a false biographical fact and loses the pun.
findings.rationale: 사천성 simultaneously means Sichuan Province in context and names a tile-matching game familiar to Korean students; Taekyung is making a wordplay-driven modern-world reference.
findings.replacement: “Sichuan Province is fun, isn’t it? I used to play it all the time during evening self-study.[^3]”

findings.current: [^3]: “Evening self-study” refers to the after-school study sessions traditionally held in Korean schools.
findings.defect: The footnote explains only evening self-study and omits the culturally specific 사천성 double meaning that is essential to understanding the joke.
findings.rationale: The revised note explains both elements needed to understand why Taekyung says he used to “play” Sichuan Province during evening self-study.
findings.replacement: [^3]: In Korean, “Sichuan Province” (*Sacheonseong*) is also the name of a tile-matching game; *yaja* refers to school-supervised evening self-study.

summary: The draft contains one critical mistranslation that turns a game-related pun into a false biographical statement, along with hierarchy, attribution, formatting, and prose issues.
